chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Mansur from al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I would not like to have [even] the best of comforts [and wealth] if it entails humiliating myself, and I have not swallowed anything that I liked more than the suppressed rage for which I do not retaliate against the one who caused it.'

key_terms.حُمُرُ النَّعَمِ: the best of comforts or wealth (literally: camels of wealth)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn value more than wealth and comfort?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umair and Hisham ibn al-Hakam, highlights the Ahl al-Bayt's emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as the mastery of the self (*nafs*). Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) illustrates this by valuing the 'swallowing of anger'—a deliberate act of self-restraint—above all material blessings, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that spiritual purity requires active suppression of ego-driven reactions. This practice is seen as a means of purifying the heart from the rust of resentment, aligning with the concept of *hilm* (forbearance) as a divine attribute.
